news_highlights.title: OpenAI and Anthropic cut their LLM prices by up to 80% within a few months. Why?
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Max Woolf charts how GPT-6.1 Sol and Opus 5.5 got far cheaper, mostly through lower cache-read prices, which make up 96-99% of agentic-coding tokens. Long Codex and Claude Code sessions now cost much less, but Codex's $200 tier lost half its allowance.

news_highlights.title: The State of Context Engineering
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Drew Breunig sorts agent failures into poisoning, distraction, confusion, clash and new 'context inertia', and lists the six harness fixes (loadout, quarantine, pruning, offloading, compaction). Practical advice: reset coding-agent context around 200-300K tokens.

news_highlights.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro scores 55 on Artificial Analysis, behind only Opus 5.5 (58), at $2/$10 per million tokens, with open weights promised by Nov 4. That means a near-frontier coding model you could switch to via any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or many hosts.

news_highlights.title: A 10-year-old CNN outperforms frontier LLMs for skin cancer diagnosis
news_highlights.why_it_matters: On 200 biopsy-proven lesions, a fine-tuned 2015 Inception v3 got 62% right versus 42% for GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1. A good reminder that a small specialised model can beat a general LLM, and it runs in a phone browser via WebGPU.
